fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

The cumulative exports (merchandise & services) during April-October 2026-27 are estimated at US$ 568.84 Billion, as compared to US$ 487.59 Billion in April-October 2025-26, an estimated growth of 16.66%.

The cumulative value of merchandise exports during April-October 2026-27 was US$ 309.06 Billion, as compared to US$ 253.40 Billion during April-October 2025-26, registering a positive growth of 21.96%.

The cumulative Non-Petroleum exports in April-October 2026-27 valued at US$ 259.22 Billion registered an increase of 18.01% as compared to US$ 219.66 Billion in April-October 2025-26.

Major drivers of merchandise export growth in October 2026 include Petroleum Products, Electronic Goods, Gems & Jewellery, Organic & Inorganic Chemicals, and Engineering Goods

Petroleum Products exports increased by 140.21% from US$ 3.70 Billion in October 2025 to US$ 8.89 Billion in October 2026.

Electronic Goods exports increased by 62.70% from US$ 4.08 Billion in October 2025 to US$ 6.64 Billion in October 2026.

Gems & Jewellery exports increased by 40.06% from US$ 2.29 Billion in October 2025 to US$ 3.21 Billion in October 2026

Organic & Inorganic Chemicals exports increased by 36.20% from US$ 2.12 Billion in October 2025 to US$ 2.89 Billion in October 2026.

Engineering Goods exports increased by 36.01% from US$ 9.37 Billion in October 2025 to US$ 12.74 Billion in October 2026.

13 NOV 2026 5:13PM by PIB Delhi

India’s total exports (Merchandise and Services combined) for October 2026* are estimated at US$ 89.99 Billion, registering a positive growth of 29.90 percent vis-à-vis October 2025. Total imports (Merchandise and Services combined) for October 2026* are estimated at US$ 110.07 Billion, registering a positive growth of 16.58 percent vis-à-vis October 2025.

summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
India's cumulative merchandise and services exports during April-October 2026-27 reached US$ 568.84 Billion, representing a 16.66% year-on-year growth, driven by strong performances in merchandise and services sectors. For October 2026 alone, total exports grew by 29.90% year-on-year to US$ 89.99 Billion, supported by significant demand in key product categories.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
* **Cumulative Trade (April–October 2026-27 vs. April–October 2025-26):**
  * **Total Exports (Merchandise & Services):** US$ 568.84 Billion, a 16.66% increase from US$ 487.59 Billion.
  * **Total Imports (Merchandise & Services):** US$ 662.19 Billion, a 16.00% increase from US$ 570.84 Billion.
  * **Overall Trade Balance:** A deficit of US$ 93.35 Billion, compared to a deficit of US$ 83.25 Billion in the year-ago period.
  * **Merchandise Exports:** US$ 309.06 Billion, a 21.96% increase from US$ 253.40 Billion.
  * **Merchandise Imports:** US$ 527.21 Billion, compared to US$ 452.86 Billion in the previous year.
  * **Merchandise Trade Deficit:** US$ 218.15 Billion, up from US$ 199.46 Billion during the same period last year.
  * **Services Exports:** US$ 259.78 Billion, compared to US$ 234.18 Billion.
  * **Services Imports:** US$ 134.98 Billion, compared to US$ 117.98 Billion.
  * **Services Trade Surplus:** US$ 124.80 Billion, an increase from US$ 116.21 Billion.
  * **Non-Petroleum Exports:** US$ 259.22 Billion, an 18.01% increase from US$ 219.66 Billion.
  * **Non-Petroleum & Non-Gems & Jewellery Exports:** US$ 240.73 Billion, compared to US$ 203.17 Billion in the previous year.
  * **Non-Petroleum & Non-Gems & Jewellery Imports:** US$ 350.58 Billion, compared to US$ 288.09 Billion.

* **Monthly Trade (October 2026 vs. October 2025):**
  * **Total Exports:** Estimated at US$ 89.99 Billion, a 29.90% year-on-year increase from US$ 69.27 Billion.
  * **Total Imports:** Estimated at US$ 110.07 Billion, a 16.58% year-on-year increase from US$ 94.42 Billion.
  * **Trade Balance:** A deficit of US$ 20.09 Billion, compared to a deficit of US$ 25.15 Billion in October 2025.
  * **Merchandise Exports:** US$ 49.47 Billion, compared to US$ 34.11 Billion in October 2025.
  * **Merchandise Imports:** US$ 89.35 Billion, compared to US$ 76.69 Billion in October 2025.
  * **Services Exports (Estimated):** US$ 40.51 Billion, compared to US$ 35.17 Billion in October 2025.
  * **Services Imports (Estimated):** US$ 20.72 Billion, compared to US$ 17.73 Billion in October 2025.
  * **Non-Petroleum & Non-Gems & Jewellery Exports:** US$ 37.38 Billion, compared to US$ 28.11 Billion in October 2025.
  * **Non-Petroleum & Non-Gems & Jewellery Imports:** US$ 57.35 Billion, compared to US$ 43.42 Billion in October 2025.

* **Key Export Growth Drivers (October 2026 YoY):**
  * **Petroleum Products:** Increased by 140.21% to US$ 8.89 Billion (from US$ 3.70 Billion in October 2025).
  * **Electronic Goods:** Increased by 62.70% to US$ 6.64 Billion (from US$ 4.08 Billion).
  * **Gems & Jewellery:** Increased by 40.06% to US$ 3.21 Billion (from US$ 2.29 Billion).
  * **Organic & Inorganic Chemicals:** Increased by 36.20% to US$ 2.89 Billion (from US$ 2.12 Billion).
  * **Engineering Goods:** Increased by 36.01% to US$ 12.74 Billion (from US$ 9.37 Billion).
  * **Other Notable Sectors:** Other Cereals (+87.47%), Oil Meals (+85.55%), Handicrafts Excl. Hand Made Carpet (+55.22%), Cereal Preparations & Miscellaneous Processed Items (+37.4%), Plastic & Linoleum (+36.28%), Meat, Dairy & Poultry Products (+34.87%), Jute Mfg. Including Floor Covering (+30.59%), Cotton Yarn/Fabs./Made-Ups, Handloom Products Etc. (+29.96%), Man-Made Yarn/Fabs./Made-Ups Etc. (+23.89%), Tea (+23.04%), Carpet (+20.64%), Rmg Of All Textiles (+20.33%), Rice (+18.39%), Marine Products (+13.76%), Leather & Leather Products (+12.73%), Mica, Coal & Other Ores, Minerals Including Processed Minerals (+12.29%), Drugs & Pharmaceuticals (+10.55%), Spices (+9.11%), Coffee (+8.51%), Ceramic Products & Glassware (+4.88%), and Fruits & Vegetables (+1.84%).

* **Methodological Notes:**
  * Services sector data for October 2026 is an estimation, as the latest released RBI data is for September 2026.
  * Data for April-October 2025-26 and April-June 2026-27 has been revised on a pro-rata basis using quarterly balance of payments data.
